places.name: Love Lake
places.description: Two man-made lakes shaped like interlocking hearts in the Al Qudra desert, ringed by trees and walking paths. Swans and other birds live here; good for a picnic, a jog or a sunset visit. No swimming. Reachable by normal car; close to the Al Qudra cycle track.

places.name: Mushrif Park Hiking Trail
places.description: A free 9.7 km hiking trail through the forest of Mushrif National Park, with wooden bridges, stairways, sculptures and rest areas. An 8.3 km recreational loop for beginners plus a 1.4 km sports section. Children 12–15 only with an adult.

places.name: Hatta Kayak
places.description: Kayaks, water bikes, pedal and donut boats on the turquoise lake of Hatta Dam, surrounded by the Hajar Mountains. Single kayaks from 16 years; double kayaks take two adults and a small child. Dogs allowed in a life vest.

places.name: Cat Cafe Vibrissae
places.description: A cat café where you sit with a dozen-plus resident cats over coffee. Day passes and private sessions; the cats are vet-checked and not for adoption, and you cannot bring your own pet. Branches in Al Safa, Creek Harbour and Mirdif.

places.name: Wasit Nature Reserve
places.description: Wetland reserve with coastal dunes, salt flats, ponds and a lake, home to more than 200 bird species. Eight bird hides with binoculars; flamingos and Arabian oryx can be seen. Aga Khan Award-winning visitor centre. Closed on Sundays.

places.name: Arabia's Wildlife Centre
places.description: Indoor and landscaped enclosures with rare Arabian animals, including the Arabian leopard and the oryx. Part of Sharjah Desert Park, 30 km east of the city, next to the Natural History Museum, botanical garden and Children's Farm.

places.name: Children's Farm (Sharjah Desert Park)
places.description: Small farm with camels, donkeys, Arabian horses, ponies, cows, goats and sheep plus a duck pond. Kids can feed the animals and ride ponies or camels. Inside Sharjah Desert Park, about 30 km east of the city.

places.name: Al Madam Buried Village
places.description: An abandoned 1970s housing village being slowly swallowed by desert dunes near Al Madam – a favourite spot for exploring and photography. Sand fills the houses and the small mosque. Best around sunrise or late afternoon.

places.name: Al Khor Kayak (Al Rafisah Dam)
places.description: Kayaks, pedal boats and donut boats on the lake of Al Rafisah Dam in the Hajar Mountains near Khor Fakkan. Fish and birds in the water; gazelles on the slopes. Open 7am–9pm; a single kayak with unlimited time was AED 40 on the official page.

places.name: Sira Khorfakkan (Shark Island)
places.description: A small rocky island a short boat ride from Khor Fakkan beach, known for snorkelling and scuba diving among coral and fish. Boats and dive trips leave from Khor Fakkan; you can also kayak around it.

places.name: Masaar Track
places.description: A 6.6 km looped cycling circuit through the woodland of the Masaar community, with underpasses and a bridge. Lit and open 24 hours. The Loop hub next to it has bike rental, repairs and a café.

places.name: Al Dhaid Fort
places.description: A square fort built around 1820 beside the old falaj water channel of the Al Dhaid oasis, where caravans once stopped for water. Its rooms now hold exhibits on the town's history and heritage.

places.name: Souq Sharia't Al Dhaid
places.description: A heritage-style market in the heart of the Al Dhaid oasis, on the spot where trade caravans used to rest. Local crafts, produce and food in traditional Emirati architecture.

places.name: Souk Sharq
places.description: Khor Fakkan's old market, rebuilt in its original style, with heritage crafts, souvenirs and a Traditional Crafts Museum. A good stop after the beach or the waterfall.

places.name: Al Hamriyah Beach
places.description: A family public beach with soft white sand, a children's play area, toilets and parking, designed to be accessible for people with disabilities.
